name: Bengaluru
title: Bengaluru: who is doing what about heat?
scope: Organisations and activities identified in public sources, read between 24 and 28 November 2026. It is not a complete list of everyone working on heat in Bengaluru, and no organisation was contacted. Common Shade is not a member, partner or representative of the Bengaluru Heat Collective.

orientation.text: In July 2026 the city recorded its hottest July day on record. The response so far is a mix: a new coalition of research, worker and civic groups, ward climate plans with first budgets, a national heat pilot run through one city corporation, and seasonal cooling centres and kits for outdoor workers. Most of it is planned or in its first season; little has been evaluated.

orgs.name: ARTPARK
orgs.summary: Builds sub-district heat-risk forecasts with Karnataka's disaster monitoring centre, disaster management authority and health department.
unknowns: Whether the heat forecasts are in routine use, by whom, and how accurate they have been.
Whether any public view of the forecasts exists.
An earlier news report gave a different forecast horizon from ARTPARK's own page; it was not read for this profile.
orgs.outside: Its other public-health programmes (dengue, One Health, maternal health) are separate and are not counted here.

orgs.name: Bengaluru Sustainability Forum
orgs.summary: An inter-institutional forum whose small grants support heat work, including a domestic-worker heat project, and which supported the apartment workers' Heat Safety Charter.
unknowns: The amounts of its heat-related grants.
What its role in the Collective is beyond founding membership.

orgs.name: C40 Cities
aliases: C40 Cities South and West Asia
orgs.based: International, with a South and West Asia office
orgs.summary: Commissioned technical assistance for two high impact heat actions in Bengaluru wards with the Greater Bengaluru Authority, and joined a cooling kits pilot for outdoor workers.
unknowns: Which two high impact actions were chosen, and whether their project reports were delivered by the planned end of March 2026.

orgs.name: CSTEP
aliases: Center for Study of Science, Technology and Policy
orgs.summary: Developing an ecosystem-based adaptation tool for Bengaluru that maps heatwave and flood risk, and part of the ward climate plan working group.
unknowns: When DEFT will be public, and in what form.
Whether BHRIGU's six urbanscapes include Bengaluru.
orgs.outside: BHRIGU, its national heat programme, plans an open National Heat Insights Explorer; Bengaluru is not named as one of its places.

orgs.name: Hasiru Dala
orgs.summary: Works with waste pickers; co-authored a survey of heat's effect on waste workers' health and income, joined a cooling kits pilot and is in the ward climate plan working group.
unknowns: Which of the similarly named Hasiru Dala entities is the member. The sources name only Hasiru Dala.
Whether the survey's recommendations have been taken up.

orgs.name: HeatWatch
orgs.summary: Researches heat and workers in Bengaluru: a waste-worker survey with Hasiru Dala, a heat charter for apartment workers with the apartment federation, domestic-worker research and a campaign to keep parks open in the heat.
unknowns: How many apartment complexes have adopted the charter.
orgs.outside: Its garment-worker dashboard and garment fieldwork cover factories outside Bengaluru.

orgs.name: Jan Sahas
orgs.summary: Initiated the Migrants Resilience Collaborative, which ran three cooling centres for outdoor workers in Bengaluru in 2026, and is in the ward climate plan working group.
unknowns: How many workers used the Bengaluru centres; the published figures are national.

orgs.name: KHPT
orgs.summary: Describes itself as a founding partner of the Collective. A separate Bengaluru heat project was not identified in the sources reviewed.
unknowns: What KHPT will contribute to the Collective's health and community work.

orgs.name: NIMHANS
aliases: National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences
orgs.summary: Founding membership verified; a separate Bengaluru heat project was not identified in the sources reviewed.
unknowns: Whether NIMHANS will lead or join any heat and mental health work in the Collective. Membership does not establish a role.

orgs.name: Socratus
orgs.summary: Runs community engagement through art and conversation, including focus groups with workers under Bengaluru Sustainability Forum's Climate Charche, and is in the ward climate plan working group.
unknowns: Its legal name: sources use four variants.

orgs.name: WRI India
orgs.summary: Steered the Begur ward climate plan's enabling work and the ward plan working group, and published the Collective's launch release and partner updates.
unknowns: Whether WRI India holds any coordinating role in the Collective. No source names a lead or secretariat.

orgs.name: Sensing Local
orgs.summary: Not a member of the Collective. Joined the cooling kits pilot and the ward climate plan working group.

orgs.name: WELL Labs
orgs.summary: Not a member of the Collective. A technical partner for the city climate plan's water work and part of the ward plan working group.

orgs.name: Bangalore Apartment Federation
orgs.summary: Not a member of the Collective. Developed the Heat Safety Charter for apartment workers with HeatWatch Foundation.
unknowns: How the federation is promoting the charter among member apartments.

authorities.name: Greater Bengaluru Authority
authorities.role: City-wide authority over five city corporations (Bengaluru Central, North, South, East and West) since September 2025; its Climate Action Cell leads the ward climate plans.

authorities.name: Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike
authorities.role: The city's former municipal corporation, before the Greater Bengaluru Authority and its five corporations (September 2025). Its name is kept for older records, such as the 2025-26 climate earmark.

authorities.name: Bengaluru North City Corporation
authorities.role: Submitted the city's proposal under the national heat resilience pilot; plans roof coating demonstrations; most cooling kits went to its workers.

authorities.name: Bengaluru South City Corporation
authorities.role: Announced ₹2 crore for phased implementation of the Begur ward climate plan.

authorities.name: Bengaluru Central City Corporation
authorities.role: Received the completed Shantinagar ward climate plan.

authorities.name: National Institute of Urban Affairs (Climate Centre for Cities)
authorities.role: Runs the Building Heat Resilient Cities pilot under AMRUT 2.0 of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, in which Bengaluru takes part.

authorities.name: Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre
authorities.role: Named by ARTPARK as a partner in its heat-risk forecasts.

authorities.name: Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority
authorities.role: Named by ARTPARK as a partner in its heat-risk forecasts.

authorities.name: Department of Health, Government of Karnataka
authorities.role: Named by ARTPARK as a partner in its heat-risk forecasts.

authorities.name: India Meteorological Department
authorities.role: Runs the city observatory whose records the July 2026 temperature figures come from.

priorities.text: Understanding heat and its spatial dimensions to inform policy and investment

priorities.short: Cooling infrastructure and the built environment

priorities.text: Strengthening relief and resilience measures for vulnerable communities
priorities.short: Worker and community protection and health

governance.not_found: No secretariat, lead organisation, workstream leads, legal status or public contact address for the Collective was found in the sources reviewed. Its charter and strategy note were not found published.

activities.title: Ward climate action plans in five pilot wards
activities.desc: Plans that list climate projects ward by ward, built with public consultations in Shantinagar, Jakkur, Begur, Vijinapura and Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar. Heat is not one of their sectors, but heat maps informed them and Begur's plan includes heat proofing of buildings.
collaborators: anchored the drafting (Shantinagar) and steered the enabling work (Begur)
working group: anchors the energy sector
activities.place: Five pilot wards, one in each zone
outputs: Public consultations held in all five pilot wards
Shantinagar's plan completed and submitted to the Climate Action Cell and Bengaluru Central City Corporation
A pipeline of 302 projects submitted to the South and North corporations for 2026-27

equity.consulted: Informal workers, waste workers and migrants took part in the ward consultations.
equity.receiving: Not yet: projects are at the proposal and budget stage.

related: Practical actions for markets and neighbourhoods

activities.title: First budget for a ward climate plan: Begur
activities.desc: Bengaluru South City Corporation announced money for phased implementation of the Begur ward plan, covering heat proofing of buildings, blue-green schools and groundwater recharge.
outputs: ₹2 crore announced as allocated, described as a starting point and not a final budget

activities.title: National heat resilience pilot through North City Corporation
activities.desc: Bengaluru takes part in the Building Heat Resilient Cities Programme under AMRUT 2.0, with a proposal submitted by Bengaluru North City Corporation. Planned measures include roof coating demonstrations on corporation buildings and protective gear for outdoor informal workers.
outputs: ₹5 crore described as allocated by the pilot, ₹1 crore of it for vulnerable populations
activities.evaluation: Not evaluated; no installation or distribution under the pilot found reported.

activities.title: Cooling centres for outdoor workers
activities.desc: Three seasonal centres with drinking water, ORS, coolers, cots and first aid: at a construction site in Whitefield, in Greater Bengaluru Authority facilities in Vidyaranyapura and above an Anganwadi in Allalasandra. Staff also helped workers apply for welfare cards and benefits.
activities.lead_note: Run by the Migrants Resilience Collaborative, which Jan Sahas initiated.
collaborators: hosts the Vidyaranyapura centre in its facilities
outputs: Three centres open from 10 April to the first week of July 2026
Help with construction welfare cards, Ayushman and e-Shram registration (staff figures)
activities.evaluation: Not evaluated; accounts come from workers, staff and the organisers.

equity.receiving: Construction workers, migrant workers and pourakarmikas used the centres.

related: Practical actions for outdoor and hot workplaces

activities.title: Cooling kits for outdoor public workers
activities.desc: Kits with a sun hat, cooling sleeves and an insulated bottle, plus shared neck fans, given to ASHAs, pourakarmikas, dry waste collection centre workers and traffic police, mostly in North City Corporation. The team proposed turning 63 Indira canteens into cooling centres during heat alerts.
collaborators: where most kits went; named for scale-up
outputs: A proposal to use 63 Indira canteens as cooling centres during heat alerts
activities.evaluation: An impact report was being prepared; not published when checked.
related: Practical actions for outdoor and hot workplaces

activities.title: How heat hits waste workers' health and income
activities.desc: A survey of 154 waste workers on access to water and toilets, symptoms, lost income and medical costs in the heat.
activities.evaluation: A survey of the harm, not an evaluation of any measure.

equity.mentioned: 98 of the 154 respondents were women; over 60% belonged to Scheduled Castes.

activities.title: A heat safety charter for apartment workers
activities.desc: Measures apartment communities can adopt in extreme heat for the people who work there, from domestic and housekeeping staff to security guards, gardeners, delivery workers and drivers, in English, Kannada and Hindi.
activities.evaluation: No adoption figures or evaluation found.

activities.title: Domestic workers and heat
activities.desc: Participatory research, workshops and a replication playbook with domestic workers, unions and resident associations, alongside HeatWatch's ongoing work with the Domestic Workers Union.
outputs: Progress report (February 2026) and final report linked from the project page

equity.consulted: Domestic workers, their unions and resident associations.

activities.title: #OpenOurParks: parks as cool places in the day
activities.desc: Volunteers audited parks closed between 11 AM and 4 PM and asked for longer hours and for parks to count as cooling and resting spaces.
outputs: Park audits and a representation to an elected representative

activities.title: Climate Charche: workers' conversations on climate
activities.desc: Focus groups with domestic, gig and migrant workers, pourakarmikas and ASHA workers, through art and conversation; water was the main theme, heat a secondary one.

activities.title: Two high impact heat actions for Bengaluru wards
activities.desc: Technical assistance commissioned to choose two high impact actions for urban heat in identified wards and write detailed project reports, with the Greater Bengaluru Authority.

activities.title: Sub-district heat-risk forecasts
activities.desc: Heat-risk predictions for areas smaller than a district, up to seven days ahead, built with the state's disaster monitoring centre, disaster management authority and health department.
activities.evaluation: No accuracy or use figures published on the page.

activities.title: An ecosystem-based adaptation tool for Bengaluru
activities.desc: A GIS-based tool to judge where blue-green measures could reduce heatwave and flood risk, with hyper-local risk maps and a household survey.
collaborators: funder, through the Global EbA Fund
activities.place: Bengaluru, extending to Bangalore Urban District; a workshop used Hebbal as a case
outputs: Workshops and a synthesis note; the tool itself is in development

timeline.text: HeatWatch and Hasiru Dala publish their waste-worker heat survey. The report page shows no date; the PDF on Hasiru Dala's site sits in a folder dated August 2025.
The Greater Bengaluru Authority's five city corporations come into being, after the BBMP.
A domestic-worker heat project starts, supported through Bengaluru Sustainability Forum.
Deadline for C40's request for technical assistance on two high impact heat actions; work planned for November 2025 to March 2026.
Ward climate plan consultations completed in five pilot wards; zone-wise budgets not yet released.
Cooling kits go to 202 outdoor public workers, mostly in North City Corporation.
Three cooling centres for outdoor workers open; they close in the first week of July.
Four of five corporations reported to have put about ₹52 crore towards climate action in 2026-27 budgets (not heat-specific).
After the launch, members reported to have agreed a charter and a strategy note (neither found published).
The city records 33.6°C, its hottest July day on record.

The Bengaluru Heat Collective is launched by 11 organisations. North City Corporation describes ₹5 crore under the NIUA pilot and plans roof coating demonstrations; South City Corporation announces ₹2 crore for the Begur ward plan.
The Collective reported to have begun a theory of change and strategic workplan.
Shantinagar's ward climate plan is completed and submitted to the Climate Action Cell and Bengaluru Central City Corporation.

gaps: No published evaluation of any heat measure in Bengaluru was found: cooling centres, kits and plans are described by organisers or reporters.
Whether the ₹5 crore and ₹2 crore have been sanctioned, released or spent. Only statements at the launch were found.
Whether the planned roof coating demonstrations have been installed.
The Collective's charter, strategy note, workstreams and any lead or coordinator.
How many workers used Bengaluru's cooling centres; published figures are national.
Whether the ARTPARK forecasts are used by any authority, and their accuracy.
Where women, older and disabled people, and migrant workers shape decisions, as distinct from being consulted or receiving support.
The Karnataka Heat Action Plan 2026 could not be read for this profile (its server returned an error), so its arrangements for Greater Bengaluru are not described here.
Kannada-language sources were not searched systematically for this first version.

contradictions.text: Pilot wards: Mongabay India names five (one per zone); Citizen Matters, three months earlier, reported plans for ten wards across five corporations.
The ₹28 crore for climate action: described as allocated by the former body in one report and as earmarked for proposed plans in another.

Member names vary across sources: Socratus appears as Socratus, Socratus Corporation, Socratus Collective Wisdom Corporation and Socratus Foundation; Jan Sahas also as Jan Sahas Foundation and Jansahas.
KHPT describes itself joining ten organisations; WRI India counts eleven founding members including KHPT. These agree on the same eleven.

start_here.text: The Begur plan and its first budget are the most concrete ward-level starting point; the cooling kit team's proposal for Indira canteens is a ready list for heat alerts.
The waste-worker survey and the apartment workers' charter give evidence and a practical text to build on; the cooling centres show what a season of relief took.
Nothing here has been evaluated. Measuring what the centres, kits and roof coatings change for workers' health and income is an open question.
The announced allocations have no published spending record yet; following them from announcement to delivery is itself useful work.
